_meta.anti_fabrication: Every value below was written to a saved artifact by code that ran in this session. Nulls are measured absences with stated reasons, never placeholders. Each key carries `source` naming the artifact and its content hash.

verification.method: every headline value in this pack was recomputed from its source CSV and compared to the stored value
verification.csv_parsing_hazard: CRITICAL for anyone reading these CSVs: several carry provenance headers as leading '#' lines, AND several SMILES columns contain '#' (triple bonds). Passing comment='#' to pandas.read_csv truncates those rows mid-line and silently yields NaN. Strip ONLY leading comment lines: skip while line.lstrip().startswith('#'), then parse the remainder. Affected files: novelty_diffsbdd.csv (2 of 20 SMILES), boltz2_comparison.csv (1 of 7).

F1_sampler_decomposition._question: Is the 4x step advantage about path geometry, or an artifact of comparing stochastic ancestral sampling against a deterministic ODE?
F1_sampler_decomposition._answer: The 4x advantage survives with the sampler family held fixed, and the sampling-noise component is zero or negative. The chapter's claim strengthens.

crossing_flow_matching_steps.definition: first budget at which mean energy distance over seeds 0-4 falls below 0.01

crossing_ddim_eta0_steps.reason: measured absence: DDIM at eta=0 never reaches the 0.01 band within the 200 distinct noise levels available; best mean 0.07318 at 200 steps

crossing_ddim_eta0_x0clip_steps.note: with the standard x0-clipping stabiliser, DDIM does cross, at 8x flow matching's budget

step_ratio_published_claim.note: 32/8 = 4, identical to the published toy_stepcount_metrics.csv crossings (ancestral 32, euler 8) - the headline is confirmed on the pinned checkpoint

energy_at_8_steps.definition: mean over seeds 0-4, 2000 samples, energy distance = 2*E|X-Y| - E|X-X'| - E|Y-Y'| (full matrices)

eta_sweep_at_8_steps.note: monotone DECREASE as eta rises: removing sampling noise COSTS 20.8x in energy

sampling_noise_component.quantified: eta 0.0 -> 1.0 improves energy 20.8x at a fixed 8-step budget, so stochasticity helps the diffusion sampler rather than flattering flow matching

eta1_equals_ancestral_validation.note: proves the DDIM respacing is identical to the ancestral sampler's, so eta is the only difference

x0_conditioning_defect.note: why deterministic DDIM struggles on THIS ladder: terminal abar=6.07e-08 amplifies epsilon error 4058x
x0_conditioning_defect.correction_note: An earlier value of 47.37 for max_abs_x0_pred_at_8_steps did NOT reproduce and has been replaced. Recomputed from toy_ddpm_trained.pt through the DDIM eta=0 update (n=2000): the peak is 1498.3 at seed 0, 800.8 to 1754.6 across seeds 0 to 4, and all of it occurs at the terminal t=199 step where abar=6.07e-08. The amplification factor 4058 and abar_terminal do reproduce exactly. Recompute detail in handoff/x0_recompute.json.

crossing_sentence.value: flow matching crosses 0.01 at 8 steps; DDIM at no tested budget (its mean energy is still 0.073 at 200 steps); ancestral DDPM at 32.

F1_sampler_decomposition.caveat: 2-D toy, 74882-parameter MLP. Do NOT generalise 'DDIM is worse than ancestral' to production scale. The defensible claim is that the 4x advantage is not an artifact of mismatched sampler families.

F2_physical_validity._question: Does the 100% validity claim survive a physical-plausibility bar?
F2_physical_validity._answer: Graph validity holds, geometry does not. The chapter's 100% tests only the molecular graph.

pb_valid_diffsbdd.definition: PoseBusters config=dock against the full 3RFM receptor

intermolecular_checks_diffsbdd.note: minimum distance to protein, volume overlap with protein/cofactors/waters, protein-ligand max distance

strain_diffsbdd_median_kcal.definition: PoseCheck UFF strain = pose energy minus relaxed-ensemble energy, kcal/mol

strain_caffeine_kcal.note: the 3RFM co-crystal reference ligand, measured the same way

Also requested and never detected: Anionic, Cationic, CationPi, PiCation, PiStacking. Detected types: HBAcceptor, Hydrophobic, VdWContact.

top_flags.flag_name: Glaxo::I1 Aliphatic methylene chains 7 or more long

honest_framing.value: HONEST-FINDINGS, NOT VALIDATION - and the verdict differs by model. FlowMol3 earns 'our batch holds up': 12/12 pass all 11 intramolecular PoseBusters checks and 0/12 trigger any of the 55 Glaxo REOS alerts. DiffSBDD is 'here is what we found when we looked': only 15/20 are PoseBusters-valid (13/20 if the 2 ligands whose energy-ratio check cannot be evaluated are counted as failures), and every failure is INTRAMOLECULAR - bond_angles 85%, bond_lengths 90%, non-aromatic ring non-flatness 95%. All 9 ligand-protein checks pass 100%, so DiffSBDD places ligands in the pocket correctly but distorts their internal geometry. Strain energy is the sharpest result and it is not a pass/fail check at all: median UFF strain is 134.5 kcal/mol for DiffSBDD and 8.2 for FlowMol3, against 0.39 for the caffeine co-crystal pose. All 20 DiffSBDD ligands exceed caffeine, 5 exceed 300 kcal/mol, and the worst is 2600.9 - energies far above any thermally accessible conformer, meaning the strain is invisible to both the chapter's validity metric and to PoseBusters' pass/fail battery. Two further cautions: clash count does NOT discriminate (DiffSBDD median 2.5 vs caffeine 3), so it should not be cited as evidence of quality; and the ligands make few real interactions (median 0 HB acceptors, 2 hydrophobic; HBDonor was requested by prolif and detected zero times in all 21 ligands), which is the PoseCheck finding reproduced. DIRECT FLAG FOR THE CHAPTER: the reported '100% validity' for both sets is RDKit sanitization plus largest-fragment extraction. It tests only whether the molecular GRAPH is legal - valences, aromaticity, ring perception - and tests NOTHING about geometry. Both sets do score 100% on the graph-level checks here (sanitization, InChI-convertibility, connectivity, no radicals), so the claim is not wrong; it is just far weaker than it sounds, and for a pocket-conditioned generator whose whole premise is 3D placement it is the wrong bar. 100% graph validity coexists with 25% of DiffSBDD ligands failing physical geometry and a median strain 346x the co-crystal reference.

F3_boltz2_controlled_comparison._question: Did pocket-conditioned generation produce a molecule Boltz-2 calls a better binder than the unconditioned one?
F3_boltz2_controlled_comparison._answer: No. Every generated ligand falls below the 0.5 binder threshold under two independent implementations, while the known co-crystal ligand clears it.

flowmol3_unconditioned_binder_probabilit.note: the molecule from the existing section I.7 run, rescored under the identical config

pocket_conditioning_verdict.value: Pocket conditioning DID beat unconditioned generation on this metric: the best DiffSBDD ligand scores 0.444 against the FlowMol3 molecule's 0.091, a 4.9x higher binder probability. But neither clears the threshold, so the honest statement is that conditioning moved the ranking without producing a predicted binder.

config_equality.recorded_difference: the hosted NIM received the top-1024 MSA records against the pinned run's full 17819
config_equality.receptor_vs_target_note: The 412 aa figure is the full UniProt P29274 sequence used as the Boltz-2 co-folding target. It is NOT the crystallized 3RFM construct, which contains 291 ordered residues (chain A, 7 to 305 with a gap at 150 to 157, 2250 protein atoms) and is what the PoseBusters and PoseCheck pocket work uses. Two different entities.

interpretation_constraint.value: affinity_pred_value is Boltz-2's log10(IC50 in uM) regression head and is only meaningful for molecules the binary head calls binders. NONE of the generated ligands clear 0.5, so converting their pred_value into an IC50 would be exactly the off-label use the chapter was corrected on. The comparison is a RANKING result, not a potency prediction.
interpretation_constraint.note: THIS IS THE OFF-LABEL GUARD. Do not convert any generated ligand's affinity_pred_value into an IC50.

runtimes.note: The hosted NIM was 4.50x faster per ligand (sum of per-ligand walls: 1065.0 s pinned vs 236.9 s hosted; means 152.1 s vs 33.8 s, the same ratio), at a depth-1024 MSA against the pinned run's 17,819. Note that 1069 s is the Modal JOB wall, which includes container start and model load, so it is not the right numerator for a per-ligand speedup; dividing it by the hosted total gives 4.51x, essentially the same figure. An earlier draft of this pack stated 'about 6x', which does not follow from any ratio of these measurements and has been corrected.

offlabel_evidence.note: Direct evidence that affinity_pred_value is not calibrated below the 0.5 gate: the molecule the binary head rejects gets an implied IC50 nearly 2x TIGHTER than the co-crystal ligand it accepts.

F4_novelty_and_diversity._question: Is 0.21 median Tanimoto to caffeine really novelty, and what fingerprint produced 0.809 diversity?
F4_novelty_and_diversity._answer: 0.21 is dissimilarity to the reference ligand, not novelty. Against the training corpus, similarity runs 2.2x higher. The 0.809 is reproducible only under RDKit's topological fingerprint; Morgan gives 0.918.

value.verdict: REPRODUCED EXACTLY (bit-for-bit) with Chem.RDKFingerprint at RDKit defaults over the 20 valid DiffSBDD molecules, formula '1 - mean pairwise Tanimoto over valid molecules'. This pins the published number's provenance.
value.why_it_matters: Under Morgan r=2/2048 the same batch scores 0.9175 rather than 0.8090 (+0.1085); the fingerprint choice must be stated or the number is not reproducible.

diversity_diffsbdd.definition: 1 - mean pairwise Tanimoto over valid molecules
diversity_diffsbdd.fingerprint_note: the published 0.809 is the RDKit topological value: Chem.RDKFingerprint(mol) at defaults (fpSize=2048, minPath=1, maxPath=7, nBitsPerHash=2). It is a path-based fingerprint; radius is not one of its parameters.

diffsbdd.definition: n_distinct_canonical_SMILES / n_valid_molecules (isomeric canonical SMILES, stereo retained)

flowmol3.definition: n_distinct_canonical_SMILES / n_valid_molecules (isomeric canonical SMILES, stereo retained)

median_max_tanimoto_vs_training_corpus.definition: per-ligand MAXIMUM Tanimoto to the sampled training corpus, then the MEDIAN of those maxima
median_max_tanimoto_vs_training_corpus.caveat: LOWER BOUND. The saturation check shows median-of-max still climbing with corpus size and not plateaued; the full corpora are 1.5-2 orders of magnitude larger than these samples.

confirmed_train_split_subset.note: restricted to ligands verified present in DiffSBDD's own published train split, so this subset needs no 'documented public preprocessing' hedge

median_tanimoto_vs_caffeine.note: reproduces the chapter's published 0.21 under the fingerprint the chapter used

value._summary: Novelty measured against the training corpus is uniformly and substantially WORSE (higher similarity) than dissimilarity to caffeine, across both batches and both fingerprints. DiffSBDD: median nearest-training-neighbour Tanimoto 0.466 vs 0.212 to caffeine (2.2x higher, +0.254 absolute) under the chapter's own RDKFingerprint. FlowMol3: 0.584 vs 0.249 (2.3x). Under Morgan r=2 the ratio widens to 3.9x for FlowMol3. Because median-of-max has not saturated at these corpus sizes, all training-proximity figures are lower bounds. The chapter's 0.21 'novelty' number therefore measures dissimilarity to one reference ligand and says nothing about training-set memorisation; the corpus-based figures are the ones that speak to the sidebar's claim.

F5_model_inventory._question: What are the real licences, runtimes and versions behind the models the chapter uses?
F5_model_inventory._answer: Four cases where the weights licence differs from the code licence, one of them unstated entirely. Six runtimes are unrecoverable and recorded as null.

value: FlowMol3
DiffSBDD
Boltz-2 via hosted NIM
DiffDock via hosted NIM
weights_more_restrictive_than_code.priority: FlowMol3 is the highest-priority fix: the chapter must not imply its weights are MIT

value: FlowMol3 WEIGHTS LICENCE IS UNSTATED. The weights ship from a bare HTTP directory listing at bits.csb.pitt.edu whose readme.md documents layout and a wget command only; a regex for licence/copyright/terms over that readme returns zero matches. The repo's MIT LICENSE covers source, not the separately-hosted checkpoints. The chapter should not imply FlowMol3 weights are MIT.
DiffSBDD weights are CC-BY-4.0 while its code is MIT (Zenodo 8183747). Attribution-on-redistribution applies to the weights and their adaptations; MIT's notice clause is not the same obligation.

Boltz-2 reached through the hosted NIM is NOT MIT-licensed to the reader. NVIDIA's API Trial Terms of Service limit use to internal testing and evaluation, not production, absent a paid Subscription, and the Community Model License forbids using the model or its outputs to develop or improve other AI models without written NVIDIA approval. The identical model from GitHub/HuggingFace is MIT for academic and commercial use. Same science, different rights, depending only on how you call it.

The DiffDock NIM does not serve the MIT repo's weights. Its model card states the served model was trained by NVIDIA on PLINDER + SAIR (486,000 complexes); the MIT link is 'Additional Information' about architecture provenance. Chapter results from this endpoint are not reproducible from gcorso/DiffDock checkpoints.

Both NIM model cards name their governing model licence INCONSISTENTLY between the card body and the page banner (Boltz-2: 'Open Model Agreement' vs 'Community Model License'; DiffDock: 'Open Model License' vs 'AI Foundation Models Community License'). These differ materially - the Open Model License is permissive with a NOTICE requirement, the Community licence adds the no-training-other-models restriction and an AI Enterprise requirement for production. A reader cannot resolve which controls from the page alone.

FlowMol3's observed timestep sweep took 1240.3 s (20.7 min) on 8-core CPU, not the '~90 min CPU' recorded in intermediates_inventory.json. The 90 min figure was a pre-run planning estimate made when the batch was still 16-20 molecules; the shipped run used 12. Cite 20.7 min.

RFdiffusion is the only model in the table whose licence explicitly covers its weights, and it is BSD rather than MIT. Its LICENSE says the copyright and licence 'covers both the source code and model weights referenced for download in the README file.'

ProteinMPNN and ESMFold have NO separable runtimes: they ran fused with the scRMSD computation in one Modal job (340.087 s for 24 backbones x 4 sequences). The chapter must not attribute a per-model time to either.

Two RFdiffusion/Boltz-2 numbers exist per run and both are real but measure different scopes: in-job wall clock (artifact job_wall_s, Modal container time) vs scheduler end-to-end (compute ledger). Boltz-2 MSA run = 161 s in-job vs 212 s end-to-end. State which is meant.

The DiffSBDD checkpoint used is one of eight in Zenodo 8183747 (sizes 16.3-77.6 MB). Naming only 'the DiffSBDD checkpoint' is ambiguous; crossdocked_fullatom_cond.ckpt is the one behind the chapter's figures.

The card states the served model is 'trained by NVIDIA using PLINDER and SAIR', reusing the MIT architecture - so results from this endpoint are not reproducible from the gcorso/DiffDock checkpoints, and the MIT reference is only 'Additional Information' about the architecture's provenance. The card does say 'ready for commercial and non-commercial use', but the trial API it is served over is testing-and-evaluation-only absent a subscription. NVIDIA's Open Model License (card body) is the permissive one - commercially usable, derivatives allowed, with a 'Licensed by NVIDIA Corporation under the NVIDIA Open Model License' NOTICE requirement - whereas the AI Foundation Models Community License named in the banner is the restrictive one. A reader cannot tell from the page which controls; that ambiguity is the finding.

F6_redocking_cross_check._question: Does an independent docking method reproduce the generator's own pose? (new experiment added this pass)
F6_redocking_cross_check._answer: No, and the two pose sources fail the physical checks in opposite ways.

rmsd_top_pose_median_A.definition: symmetry-corrected RMSD between the generator's pose and DiffDock's top-ranked pose, no alignment (both already in the receptor frame)

same_pocket_though.note: the disagreement is about pose detail inside the site, not about finding the site

pb_valid_comparison.note: the identical PoseBusters dock-config bar applied to both sources

opposite_failure_modes.value: The two pose sources fail in OPPOSITE ways. DiffSBDD's own poses are placed cleanly relative to the protein (100% on every intermolecular check) but carry internal geometry strain (bond_angles 85%, bond_lengths 90%). DiffDock's re-docked poses have clean internal geometry (100% bond lengths and angles, since DiffDock keeps a valid RDKit conformer and only moves it rigidly plus torsions) but violate minimum_distance_to_protein on 55% of ligands.

verdict.value: Independent docking does NOT reproduce the generator's placement. No ligand's top-ranked DiffDock pose lands within 2 A of the DiffSBDD pose (median 4.39 A), and only 2 of 20 have ANY of 10 poses within 2 A. Re-docked poses do stay in the same pocket (19/20 centroids within 5 A of the co-crystal caffeine, median 1.77 A vs 0.63 A for the generated poses), so the disagreement is about pose detail inside the site, not about finding the site. DiffDock's own confidence is low: median top-pose confidence 0.10, and 7 of 20 negative.

framing_caveat.value: This is a NEW experiment the current chapter does not set up. It is also not a redocking-accuracy benchmark: there is no experimental pose for a de novo ligand, so neither source can be called correct. The defensible claim is agreement/disagreement between two independent methods, not accuracy.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: HIGH - legal claim in a commercially published book
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "FlowMol3 ships pretrained weights under a permissive MIT license, and the library fetches them for us on first use."
_contradictions_with_current_draft.location: section I.3, 'Loading and Sampling from a Pretrained Model'
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: The FlowMol repo's LICENSE is MIT and covers the SOURCE. The weights are served separately from a bare HTTP directory at bits.csb.pitt.edu/files/FlowMol/trained_models_v3.1/. Its readme.md (2283 bytes, fetched and grepped this session) contains ZERO occurrences of licence, copyright, terms, permission or redistribut; the directory listing contains no LICENSE file. The weights licence is UNSTATED, not MIT.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Say the CODE is MIT and that the pretrained weights are distributed separately without an accompanying licence statement. Do not attribute MIT to the weights.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: HIGH - the metric is not what the word means
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "Panel (c) shows novelty as Tanimoto similarity to caffeine" and "On novelty, the result is what we hoped for: a median Tanimoto similarity to caffeine of just 0.21"
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: 0.21 reproduces exactly (0.2121 recomputed) but measures dissimilarity to the REFERENCE LIGAND. Against a sampled training corpus, median-of-max Tanimoto is 0.4664 under the same fingerprint, 2.2x higher; 0.4453 restricted to ligands confirmed in DiffSBDD's own published train split. Under Morgan r=2 the gap is 2.4x. Median-of-max is still climbing with corpus size, so those are lower bounds.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Call 0.21 what it is (dissimilarity to the reference ligand) and add the corpus comparison as the novelty claim. This makes the chapter's own sidebar argument land harder.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "a pairwise diversity of 0.809 means the model is not quietly drawing the same molecule twenty times"
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: 0.8089776623453144 reproduces bit-for-bit, but ONLY under Chem.RDKFingerprint at RDKit defaults (fpSize=2048, minPath=1, maxPath=7, nBitsPerHash=2) - a path-based fingerprint. Under Morgan r=2/2048, which is what a reader would assume for a diversity number, the same batch scores 0.9175.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Name the fingerprint and the formula in the sentence or a footnote. The number is correct; it is just not reproducible without its definition.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: MEDIUM - the claim is narrower than the sentence
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "all 20 are chemically valid (100%), and every one is a single connected molecule rather than a scatter of disconnected pieces (100% connected)"
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: Both hold, and PoseBusters confirms all_atoms_connected at 100%. But those checks test the molecular GRAPH. On the physical bar, 15 of 20 DiffSBDD ligands pass the full protein-aware suite (bond_angles 85%, bond_lengths 90%), and UFF strain has a median of 134.5 kcal/mol against the co-crystal caffeine's 0.39 - 347x. FlowMol3's batch passes 12/12 with a median strain of 8.2.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Keep the 100% but scope it to graph validity, then add the physical-plausibility result. The chapter's own 'valid and connected is a low bar' sentence already sets this up.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: MEDIUM - number does not match its own source
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "the diffusion model at the same eight steps is still stranded at 0.388, more than thirty times larger" and "the diffusion samples at the same budget (0.371)"
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: 0.371 is the published CSV's seed-mean and 0.388 its seed-3 value, so the draft is internally consistent with toy_stepcount_metrics.csv. But the PINNED checkpoint gives 0.0407 at 8 steps - roughly 9x lower. The published sweep trained its DDPM inline; the cached checkpoint is a different, better-converged run. Separately, the PUBLISHED FIGURE's panel (b) label reads 0.10, which matches no seed in its own CSV (range 0.335-0.403).
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Cite the new drift-free assets/toy_sampler_sweep.csv and update the matched-budget numbers to 0.041 (ancestral) against 0.010 (flow matching), a ~4x gap at 8 steps rather than 30x. The 4x CROSSING claim is unaffected and confirmed.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: LOW - framing, and the fix strengthens the claim
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "flow matching hit target quality in about 8 steps against diffusion's 32, a roughly fourfold saving"
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: Confirmed exactly on the pinned checkpoint (crossings 8 and 32). The reviewer's concern was that the comparison mixes a stochastic diffusion sampler with a deterministic ODE. Measured: making the diffusion sampler deterministic does NOT shrink the gap - DDIM at eta=0 never reaches the band within 200 levels, and the eta sweep shows removing noise COSTS 20.8x at a fixed 8-step budget.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Keep 4x and add one sentence: the advantage survives holding the sampler family fixed, so it is about path geometry rather than an artifact of comparing sampler families.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: INFO - not in the draft, needed before the new figure lands
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: (no current text) - the chapter's Boltz-2 section reports the FlowMol3 ligand's numbers but does not state a binder threshold
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: Across 7 molecules under two independent Boltz-2 implementations, ONLY the co-crystal caffeine clears the 0.5 binder threshold (0.622/0.617). The best generated ligand reaches 0.444. Pocket conditioning did beat unconditioned generation 4.9x on this metric (0.444 vs 0.091) without producing a predicted binder.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: State the threshold explicitly and keep the ranking-not-potency guard: affinity_pred_value must not be converted to an IC50 for molecules the binary head does not call binders.

_contradictions_with_current_draft.severity: HIGH - prints a number that its own model says is meaningless
_contradictions_with_current_draft.chapter_text: "The affinity head (panel b) returns a binder probability of just 0.09, well below the 0.5 call line, and a predicted IC50 of roughly 15 uM (log10 IC50/uM = 1.17)."
_contradictions_with_current_draft.location: section I.7, paragraph after Figure I.14
_contradictions_with_current_draft.what_we_found: Both numbers reproduce (0.0928 and 1.1657 from boltz_a2a_msa_summary.json; our independent rerun gives 0.0906 and 1.1239). But the sentence prints the regression head's IC50 for a molecule the SAME model's binary head places below the call line, which is the off-label use the chapter was corrected on. Direct evidence that the number is meaningless there: caffeine, which the binary head DOES call a binder at 0.622, gets pred_value 1.3978 = 25.0 uM. So the non-binder's pred_value implies a TIGHTER IC50 (13.3 uM) than the real co-crystal ligand's. The regression head is not calibrated below the gate.
_contradictions_with_current_draft.fix: Keep the binder probability and DROP the IC50 conversion, or state explicitly that the regression head is not meaningful below the call line and give the caffeine comparison as the reason. Tracked change applied: the IC50 clause is deleted and replaced.
